explanation: Abolishing the Council of the Revolution meant amending the constitution, and amending it meant two thirds of the deputies. The Democratic Alliance had wanted the Council gone since before it was an alliance. The election of 2 December 1979, confirmed at the fresh election of October 1980, put it in charge of the Assembly with the standing to demand the revision. It did not have two thirds on its own. The text of 1982 was a bargain with the Socialists, and the 1979 result bought the alliance the position from which it could force that bargain.
